acceptance: The run directory and watchdog log of the 2026-11-12 cell are located and recorded (or recorded as not retained)
A test reproduces a breach after the guarded command exits 0 and asserts the documented status
A test asserts a breach during active work still makes host_lock exit 79 (make prints Error 79)
docs/agent/heavy-work.md states how a late breach is reported
description:
## Problem
On 2026-11-12, a ClickHouse TPC-H SF1 tuning-evidence cell run through make heavy-run finished with harness status completed and full results, yet the wrapper exited 79 (watchdog stopped the process tree). An agent reading only the exit status treats a good measurement as killed and retries it, wasting hours on a memory-constrained host; a CI consumer would mark it failed. The kill most likely landed during teardown (container stop, child cleanup) after the command's own work ended.

## Decision gate
Reproduce with a guarded command that finishes, then holds a child briefly during teardown while a breach is simulated through the watchdog test seams. Then decide which status is correct:
- If the guarded command's own exit status was 0 before the breach, heavy-run returns 0 and logs the late breach as a warning.
- If the breach interrupted work the command still needed (output not flushed, cleanup incomplete), keep 79 but say so in the message.

## Guardrails
- A breach during the command's active work must still exit 79.
- Do not weaken the kill rule itself (that is heavy-run-admitted-then-killed-by-foreign-memory-pressure-20261112).
- Tests use the existing watchdog test seams; no deliberate CPU or memory load.
- Retry-after-breach (heavy-run-admitted-then-killed-by-foreign-memory-pressure-20261112) must not replay a command that already exited 0.
- Exit codes: host_lock run exits 79; make heavy-run exits 2 and prints Error 79.
